G4691.as:
* σπερμολόγος, -ον (< σπέρμα, λέγω)
a seed picker;
(a) prop., of birds (Arist., Aristoph, al.);
(b) in Attic slang, of an idler who lives on scraps picked up in the agora; hence, as subst., ὁ σ., an idle babbler: .†

G4635.as:
*† σκηνοποιός, -όν (< σκηνή, ποιέω),
making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: .†

G4645.as:

to harden. Metaph., to harden, make stubborn: c. acc. pers., ; τ. καρδίας (Ps 94 (95):8), , . Pass., to become hardened: , .†

G4612.as:

G4631.as:

equipment, tackle: .†

G4636.as:
** σκῆνος, -ους, τό [in LXX: Wi 9:15 * ;]
= σκηνή,
a tent, tabernacle (C.I., 3071). Metaph., of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: , .†

G4647.as:
σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ [in LXX: Nu 33:55 (שֵׂךְ), Ho 2:6 (8) (סִיר), Ez 28:24 (סִלּוֹן), Si 43:19 * ;]
anything pointed, esp.
1. in cl., a stake
2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. c.): σ. τῇ σαρκί, (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).†

G4656.as:
σκοτόω, -ῶ (< σκότος), [in LXX for חשׁךְ, קדר, שׁחר ;]
to darken: . Metaph., of the mind : pass., (cf. σκοτίζω).†

G4696.as:
* σπίλος (Rec. σπῖλος), -ου, ὁ
1. a rock, cliff (Arist., al.).
2. In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (v. Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaph.,
(a) of moral blemish:
(b) of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l.): .†

G4689.as:
σπένδω [in LXX chiefly for נסך hi. ;]
to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., fig., σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): (v. Lft., in l.), (for exx. from π., v. Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).†

G4657.as:
**† σκύβαλον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Si 27:4 * ;]
refuse, esp. dung (v. MM, ii, iii, xxiii): .†

G4649.as:
σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for צֹפֶה ;]
1. a watcher, watchman (Ez 3:17, al.).
2. a mark on which to fix the eye (Wi 5:12, 21, al.). Metaph., of an aim or object: .†

G4658.as:
Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ
Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: .†

G4684.as:
† σπαταλάω, -ῶ (< σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, Si 27:13 *), [in LXX: Ez 16:49 (שׁקט hi.), Si 21:15 * ;]
to live riotously: , (Polyb.).†
SYN.: στρηνιάω, τρυφάω (v. Tr., Syn., § liv)

G4629.as:
* σκέπασμα, -τος, τό (< σκεπάζω, to cover),
a covering, esp. clothing: .†

G4679.as:
σοφίζω (< σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חכם ;]
to make wise, instruct: c. acc. pers., (cf. Ps 18 (19):8 (Ps 118 (119):98). As depon., -ομαι;
(a) intrans., to become wise (III Ki 4:27 ( 5:11)), Ec 2:15, and freq. in Si 7:5, al.);
(b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., (cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).†

G4695.as:
**† σπιλόω [in LXX: Wi 15:4 * ;]
to stain, spot, defile: c. acc., , .†

G4694.as:
* σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ (on the gender in Ju, l.c., v. Mayor, Ju., 41),
1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaph., of men whose conduct causes danger to others, , R, txt. (but v. infr.).
2. In late writers = σπίλος (q.v.), a spot, stain; metaph., , R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but v. supr.).†

G4667.as:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: .†

G4664.as:
*† σμαράγδινος (< σμάραγδος, q.v.),
1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11).
2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: (for the construction, v. Swete, in l.; Zorell, s.v.).†

G4604.as:
σίδηρος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;]

G4665.as:
σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ (and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Ex 28:9 (שֹׁהַם) 36:17 (39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Ez 28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;]
